For each group of environmental variables, principal components were calculated and selected until the cumulative explained variance reached 80%; these components were used as predictors in the GDM. Colour shading denotes individual principal component dimensions. Variable loadings are shown in Extended Data Fig. 7. Model statistics and predictor importance using Monte Carlo sampling with 250 permutations are reported in Supplementary Tables 2 and 3. Landscape context is represented by the mean forest cover within a 200 m concentric buffer surrounding each plot.

According to recent reports, the three taxonomic groups with the strongest explanatory power—understorey plants, fungi and bacteria—also exhibited homogenization in the agricultural land uses (Fig. 2). This pattern suggests that homogenization is driven, to a large extent, by deterministic processes associated with land-use-induced changes in the environment, including direct impacts from soil disturbance and fertilization, and indirect effects from the deliberate replacement of forest species with a single, often non-native, target crop, and an alteration of vegetation structure by establishing even-aged structure. Additionally, biotic homogenization is driven by characteristics of the surrounding landscape (Supplementary Table 3). Processes leading to biotic differentiation can also emerge from changes in vegetation structure, as observed in most canopy-dwelling groups. Thus, for many groups, homogenization and differentiation can be linked to drastic changes in habitat structure following land-use intensification30 and in the remaining surrounding forests. Still, biotic differentiation can also be only weakly related to environmental conditions and the surrounding landscape, as for leaf litter spiders, mesostigmatid mites and springtails. Thus, biotic differentiation could be more stochastic and potentially driven by disturbance, legacy effects or meta-population and meta-community dynamics that were not quantified here.

Industry observers note that our results provide detailed insights into how tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity through concurrent changes in species richness and community composition. We document pronounced declines in γ- and α-multidiversity from lowland forests to monocultures, driven primarily by aboveground taxa. The diminishing tropical (degraded) forests and traditional agroforestry systems in our study region constitute irreplaceable reservoirs of biodiversity, but their biodiversity is in peril and requires urgent conservation and restoration actions. Divergent responses between aboveground and belowground compartments underscore the need to integrate multiple taxonomic groups spanning body size and mobility. We found no evidence for consistent community homogenization with land-use intensification. Instead, consistent with previous work, we found taxon-specific and seemingly idiosyncratic patterns of both biotic homogenization and differentiation19,20,22,50, but we also revealed a systematic shift from turnover to nestedness in monocultures. Our results call for careful interpretation of spatial patterns of community homogenization and differentiation, as well as long-term monitoring, because homogenization–differentiation trends can be scale-dependent (in line with the landscape divergence hypothesis) and can differ between smallholder and industrial plantations, which are not included in our study. In addition, early stages of assemblage simplification may mask trajectories towards biotic homogenization. Overall, our results demonstrate that land-use intensification alters multidiversity across spatial scales, with ecosystem-wide consequences for biotic communities and their abiotic environment, and suggest that habitat filtering has a stronger role than neutral or dispersal processes. Effective conservation will benefit from recognizing the conservation value of traditional agricultural systems, which, in our study region, buffer the loss of multiple generalist forest species and exhibit high levels of β-diversity. These traditional agricultural systems are currently under pressure from conversion and lie outside the conservation focus and landscape planning. Furthermore, implementing sustainable management practices2,3,4 within conventional monocultures could help mitigate biodiversity losses and promote landscape differentiation in these agricultural landscapes. Differentiation across multiple taxonomic groups should not overshadow the homogenization occurring within key taxonomic groups such as bats, birds, trees and understorey plants. Therefore, there is a growing need to establish conservation priorities for focal taxonomic groups, including tailored landscape-scale solutions to maximize the γ-diversity of forest-associated biodiversity, such as conserving irreplaceable endemic species in this biodiversity hotspot.

Sources indicate that our study was conducted in the province of Jambi on the island of Sumatra, Indonesia. This tropical lowland region has undergone extensive land-use changes since the twentieth century and is a showcase of smallholder agriculture in Indonesia13,42. Two sample landscapes, ‘Harapan’ and ‘Bukit Duabelas’ (with loam and clay Acrisol soils, respectively), were selected within Jambi Province. In each landscape, four 50 m × 50 m replicate plots were established in each of the four land-use types common to the region: primary degraded forest (sensu ref. 51), jungle rubber (a traditional agroforestry system established by planting rubber trees inside secondary forest), smallholder monoculture rubber plantation, and smallholder monoculture oil palm plantation—totalling 32 plots. The number of replicate sites per land use is comparable to that of other ecological studies in tropical lowland regions52. Various measurements, such as microclimate, were taken at the plot level. Other measurements, such as most biodiversity sampling, were taken in five permanent 5 m × 5 m subplots established within each plot. All sites were selected in 2012. At this time, rubber plantations were established 7–16 years ago, and oil palm plantations were established 8–15 years ago. For jungle rubber, plots selected contained older non-rubber trees, with individual rubber trees of varying ages not planted in rows13.

In a recent development, jungle rubber, rubber and oil palm plots were owned and managed by smallholder farmers, whereas the forest plots were located in the Bukit Duabelas National Park and the Harapan Rainforest Restoration concession area (PT REKI). In our study region, smallholders generally do not cultivate food crops alongside the target cash crops examined here, with only a few exceptions8,42,43. Our study’s oil palm plots were on average surrounded by ~13.6% forest and ~61% oil palm plantations within 1 km buffers compared with ~0.45% and ~96% in industrial oil palm plantations, respectively41. Further, our oil palm plots received less herbicide (0.73 l ha−1 year−1) and fertilizer (6.6 kg N ha−1 year−1) compared with industrial oil palm plantations41 (1.12 l ha−1 year−1 and 141 kg N ha−1 year−1). Rubber and oil palm smallholder plantations represent the highest land-use intensity level among the systems included in our study. Yet land-use intensity is even higher in large-scale industrial plantations. More information on the study region, study design, land-use types and management practices of the smallholder systems is provided elsewhere8,13,42. Data compilation in these studies has also served as a basis for our study, but has been substantially expanded in recent years. For example, a multi-taxon perspective was offered in ref. 42 for 3 taxonomic groups, in ref. 13 for 9 taxonomic groups, and in ref. 8 for 14 taxonomic groups.

It has been revealed that we studied 24 different biodiversity indicators distributed from the canopy to the soil, namely: (1) ants (Hymenoptera: Formicidae), (2) beetles (Coleoptera), (3) true bugs (Hemiptera), (4) flies (Diptera)53, (5) parasitoids (parasitoid Hymenoptera), (6) spiders (Araneae), and (7) springtails (Collembola), from the canopy; (8) bats (Chiroptera), (9) birds (Aves), (10) butterflies (Lepidoptera), (11) trees (Tracheophyta), (12) understorey plants (Tracheophyta), (13) spiders, (14) beetles, and (15) ants, from the leaf litter; (16) centipedes (Chilopoda), (17) springtails, (18) mesostigmatid mites (Mesostigmata), and (19) oribatid mites (Oribatida), from the litter and soil; and (20) fungi, (21) testate amoebae, (22) protists, (23) bacteria, and (24) archaea, from the soil (Supplementary Table 4). These biodiversity indicators represent a wide spectrum of taxa, encompassing all domains of life, various trophic levels, and diverse ecological strategies, dispersal abilities and body sizes. This comprehensive dataset builds on a long-term collaborative effort that generated detailed insights into individual taxonomic groups, including species descriptions54,55,56,57,58,59, field guides60,61,62,63 and functional and trophic interactions53,64,65,66—as well as ecosystem-wide analyses and integrative studies linking ecological and socio-economic dimensions8,13,42.

According to recent reports, canopy arthropods (ants, beetles, bugs, flies, parasitoids, spiders and springtails) were collected by canopy fogging in the dry season from May to October 2013. In each of the 32 plots, 3 representative canopy locations were selected, avoiding canopy gaps and overly dense canopies. At each of the 3 locations, 16 rectangular traps (1 m × 1 m) fitted with 100 ml ethanol-filled bottles were suspended from ropes beneath the selected canopies at approximately 1.50 m. 50 ml of DECIS EC 25 (active ingredient: deltamethrine 25 g l−1), dissolved in 4 l of petroleum white oil, was applied to the target canopies from the ground using the Swingtec Swingfog SN 50. In all four land-use systems, target canopies consisted of leaves from different trees. Stunned and dead arthropods were collected from the traps up to 2 h after the complete application of the fogging mixture. Canopy fogging was conducted in the early morning, immediately after sunrise, to minimize air movement that would disperse the fog. This was done only in dry conditions, ensuring that small arthropods would not become trapped in water droplets on leaves and branches. Overall, 372,146 canopy arthropod individuals were collected this way53 and sorted into morphospecies for selected taxa. This study includes data from the following taxa: ants (Hymenoptera: Formicidae) 179 morphospecies67; beetles (Coleoptera) 397 morphospecies in 4 families (Chrysomelidae, Curculionidae, Elateridae and Staphylinidae)68; true bugs (Hemiptera) 301 morphospecies in 2 suborders (Auchenorrhyncha and Heteroptera); flies (Diptera) 483 morphospecies in 2 suborders (Brachycera and Nematocera, including Eudiptera)69; parasitoid wasps (Hymenoptera: “Parasitica”) 1,012 morphospecies in 6 families (Braconidae, Ceraphronidae, Encyrtidae, Eulophidae, Scelionidae and Platygastridae)70; spiders (Araneae) 445 morphospecies71; and springtails (Collembola) 60 morphospecies72. Recorded (morpho-)species across taxa are deposited in the http://ecotaxonomy.org database and in refs. 60,61,62.

Bats were surveyed using mist nets and harp traps between April and August 2015. We used telescopic aluminium poles to install mist nets with a total length of 48 m, as well as two harp traps (1.35 m × 1.75 m) in presumed bat flyways. Mist nets were 3 m high, with a 19-mm mesh size, and were installed at ground level or up to 3 m high, depending on plot conditions. Each plot was sampled from 17:30 to 22:00 on two consecutive nights, resulting in an average sampling effort of 1,296 m2 of mist net hours. We checked the nets and traps every 15 min until 20:00 and every 30 min thereafter. Harp traps were left on site until and checked the morning after. Captured bats were left in tissue pouches until the nets were closed. Then bat morphology was measured to identify them according to the latest bat species checklist for Sumatra73. We tagged the bats’ nails with nail polish colour codes to identify recaptures and released them afterwards. This study includes data from 20 bat species. In plot HJ3, no individuals were caught (total abundance = 0).

It has been revealed that birds were sampled with point counts74, as well as automated sound recordings, from May to July 2013. Point counts and automated sound recordings lasted 20 min and were conducted from the centre of each plot between 6:00 and 10:00. The timing of point counts alternated between early and late morning, and all plots were visited three times. The automated sound recorders (SM2+ with two SMX-II microphones, Wildlife Acoustics) were set up at ~2 m height to record at a 44.1 kHz sampling rate in stereo, simultaneously across land-use types; one recording, starting at sunrise, was used for each plot. Point count detections of individuals flying above the canopy were excluded, and unfamiliar bird calls were recorded using a Sennheiser ME-66 directional microphone. The automated sound recordings were uploaded to ecoSound-web, an online platform for ecoacoustics75, for two independent ornithologists to identify all bird calls within an estimated 35 m radius. Only bird species identified by both ornithologists in recordings of each plot were used and subsequently merged with the species list obtained from the point counts. Aural detections were confirmed with cross-checks on the Xeno-Canto online bird call database (https://xeno-canto.org/). This study encompasses data from 114 bird species. For birds, BO1_5 data were unavailable. Therefore, when analyses required non-missing values, imputation was performed by using the average from plots of the same land use within the same landscape (that is, Bukit). However, γ-diversity values for birds may be underestimated.

Recent findings suggest that butterflies (Lepidoptera: Papilionidae, Pieridae, Lycaneidae and Nymphalidae) were recorded from all 32 study plots in the dry season of 2017 between August and October. Butterflies were collected using sweep netting on three parallel 50-m transects per plot, with two transects on the outer boundaries and the third through the centre. Sweep netting was conducted once in the morning (8:00−11:00) and repeated in the afternoon (13:00−16:00). Except for two voucher specimens per collected species, all butterfly individuals were released on the evening of the sampling day. This study includes data based on butterfly specimens from 219 species76. Recorded morphospecies are deposited in the http://ecotaxonomy.org database and in ref. 63.

Plant inventories were conducted between February 2013 and August 2014, using different sampling schemes for large trees and vascular understorey plants30. All trees per plot with a diameter of ≥10 cm at a height of 1.3 m were identified. Vascular understorey plants were censused in the five 5 m × 5 m subplots per plot, including all plant individuals, such as terrestrial plants (herbs, shrubs, climbers and juvenile trees) and epiphytes growing up to 3 m above the ground. 281 tree species were present in both censuses (for large trees and understorey plants). To avoid inflating species richness, they were retained only in the matrix that included large trees. Species identification was conducted in the field if possible or otherwise based on field photographs and herbarium specimens deposited at BIOT, BO, GOET, and the herbaria at Jambi University and Harapan Rainforest (acronyms follow Index Herbarium: http://sweetgum.nybg.org/science/ih/). The number of all individuals per species and plot was used for analyses. In total, this study includes 443 tree species and 976 vascular plant species in the understorey.

Sources indicate that leaf litter was collected from three of the five subplots within each of the study plots. In each subplot, leaf litter from 1 m2 of ground was sieved using a coarse mesh (width of 2 cm). All macro-invertebrates visible to the naked eye were hand-collected from the sieved samples, stored in 65% ethanol and transported to the laboratory for identification12. Recorded (morpho-)species are deposited in the http://ecotaxonomy.org database. This study includes data on 135 morphospecies of ants, 170 morphospecies of beetles, and spider specimens from 132 morphospecies. For leaf litter spiders and leaf litter beetles, no individuals were detected in plots HO2 and BO4, respectively (total abundance = 0).

Recent findings suggest that between October and November 2013, random samples were taken from three 5 m × 5 m subplots per plot (a total of 96 samples). Samples were taken at least 2 m from the next tree or dead-wood accumulation. Each sample measured 16 cm × 16 cm and included the complete litter layer and the underlying topsoil to a depth of 5 cm, obtained using a spade. Animals were extracted using heat and stored in 70% ethanol77. This study includes data from 12 morphospecies. In plot BR2, no individuals were detected (total abundance = 0).

According to recent reports, samples were taken in October 2013. In each plot, one randomly positioned soil core (16 cm × 16 cm) was taken to a depth of 5 cm in the mineral soil. Litter and soil layers were separated in the field and extracted independently. Animals were extracted by heat for 5–10 days until the substrate was completely dry78, collected in dimethyleneglycol–water solution (1:1) and stored in 70% ethanol79. This study includes data from 58 morphospecies.

It has been revealed that three soil cores were taken in October and November 2013 from each of 32 plots. Soil cores (16 cm × 16 cm) were collected from the litter layer and the underlying soil to a depth of 5 cm. Animals were extracted under a heat gradient78, collected in dimethyleneglycol–water solution (1:1) and thereafter stored in 70% ethanol. Identification of soil mites was done on microscopic slides to (morpho)species level. Recorded (morpho)species are deposited in the http://ecotaxonomy.org database. More details are described in ref. 80. This study includes data from 110 morphospecies of mesostigmatid mites and 219 morphospecies of oribatid mites.

Soil samples were collected in October and November 2016. In three subplots (5 m × 5 m) per plot, five soil cores (15 cm depth, 4 cm diameter) were taken and pooled, yielding a total of three samples per plot. Samples were sieved (50 × 50 mm mesh) and freeze-dried. DNA extraction, sequencing, and assignment of OTUs have been described81. Data have been deposited in the Dryad repository82. This study includes data from 12,309 OTUs.

Litter and upper mineral soil samples (to a depth of 50 mm) were collected in October and November 2013 using a 50 mm diameter corer. Testate amoebae were extracted from the samples by washing 1 g dry weight sample through a 500-µm mesh and back-sieving the filtrate through a 10-µm mesh. More details are described in ref. 83. This study includes data from 190 morphospecies of testate amoebae.

Sources indicate that soil samples were collected from each study plot and processed (sieving, freeze-drying and milling) to extract DNA for protist community analysis84. This study includes data from 5,204 OTUs of protists.

Soil samples were taken at the subplot level, DNA was extracted and amplicons were generated with primer pairs targeting the 16S ribosomal RNA gene of bacteria and archaea and used to assess bacterial and archaeal community compositions separately33. This study includes data on 16,413 bacterial OTUs and 448 archaeal amplicon sequence variants. For archaea, HF3 data were unavailable. Therefore, when analyses required non-missing values, imputation was performed by using the average from plots with the same land use within the same landscape (that is, Harapan). However, γ-diversity values for archaea may be underestimated.

We consider 24 environmental variables distributed into 4 groups: microclimate, vegetation, litter and soil (Supplementary Table 5).

Meteorological stations were set up in the centre of each plot to measure hourly below-canopy air temperature and relative humidity at 2 m height between June 2013 and October 2014. Additionally, soil sensors were used to measure soil temperature and moisture at a depth of 0.3 m (ref. 85).

Recent findings suggest that different aspects of structural complexity have been measured using terrestrial laser scanning in each of the 32 plots in September and October 2016. Based on a single-scan approach, we calculated the effective number of layers, which quantifies vertical stratification86, and the stand structural complexity index87, which describes the complexity of vegetation’s three-dimensional occupation of space. We collected nine single scans, evenly distributed across each plot, and aggregated at the plot level using mean and standard deviation, the latter describing the spatial heterogeneity of vegetation structure88. Additionally, hemispherical photographs were taken at 1.2 m above the ground from 32 positions within each plot to derive canopy openness42. Fine root production was estimated by installing 16 ingrowth cores per plot8.

Aboveground litterfall was assessed by placing 16 litter traps (75 cm × 75 cm) in each plot. Traps were emptied monthly from March 2013 to April 2014. For oil palms, pruned leaves were counted, and a subsample was dried and weighed. For litter nutrients, aliquots of material from the litter–fermentation layer of all 32 plots were dried at 65 °C for 72 h, milled, and analysed for total C and N concentrations using an elemental analyser89 (Carlo Erba Instruments).

Soil sampling was conducted in 2013. Within a 50 m × 50 m area at each site, ten grid points were selected (including the five subplots), and soil samples were taken from the top 0–0.1 m depth. The ten subplots were averaged to represent each site. Soil biochemical characteristics (that is, pH, soil organic carbon (kg C m−2), total nitrogen (g N m−2), 15N natural abundance signatures (‰ 15N), effective cation exchange capacity (ECEC; mmolc m−2), base saturation (%), aluminium saturation (%) and extractable phosphorus (g P m−2)) were determined on air-dried and sieved (2 mm) soil samples. Organic carbon and total nitrogen were analysed using a CN analyser (Vario EL Cube, Elementar Analysis Systems) and 15N by isotope ratio mass spectrometry (Delta Plus, Finnigan MAT). ECEC was determined by percolating the soils with unbuffered 1 mol l−1 NH4Cl, and cations (Ca, Mg, K, Na, Al, Fe and Mn) were measured in percolates using an inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectrometer (iCAP 6300 Duo VIEW ICP Spectrometer, Thermo Fisher Scientific). Base and aluminium saturation were calculated as percentage exchangeable bases or aluminium on the ECEC. Extractable phosphorus was determined using the Bray 2 method for acidic tropical soils. Soil physical characteristics for each site included bulk density (g cm−3; core method)32,90. Soil respiration was measured monthly in 2013 using a chamber located on four subplots per plot. Gas samples were analysed using a gas chromatograph with an electron capture detector and a flame ionization detector (GC 6000 Vega Series2, Carlo Erba Instruments)91.

Sources indicate that environmental data. We conducted a principal component analysis for each group of variables, with variables transformed (when needed) and scaled. We selected the first components until the cumulative explained variance reached 80%. Variable contributions of these selected principal components are displayed in Extended Data Fig. 7.

It has been revealed that landscape data. We calculated landscape metrics within 200 m buffers around our plot centres using a manually classified land-use map derived from satellite imagery from 2016 (ref. 92). We used the R package landscapemetrics93 to calculate the mean forest coverage.

Species occurrences were calculated separately for each taxonomic group.

α- and γ-diversities. We quantified diversity using the Hill number framework, expressing it as effective species numbers, where q0 disregards species abundances and is therefore more sensitive to rare species (species richness) and q1 weights species in proportion to their abundances, favouring neither rare nor dominant species (that is, effective number of common species; Shannon diversity)94. In addition, we calculated rarefaction–extrapolation curves for the 24 taxonomy groups at plot (that is, α-diversity; Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2) and each land use (that is, γ-diversity; Supplementary Fig. 3) level using the iNEXT R package95,96.

According to recent reports, α- and γ-multidiversity. To assess the multidiversity across all 24 taxonomic groups, first, we normalized the observed effective number of species at the plot or land-use type level using the min–max scaling approach, following: y = (x − min(x))/(max(x) − min(x)), where x is the set of observed effective number of species. The normalized effective number of species (y) ranges between 0 and 1, with 0 referring to the lowest observed value and 1 to the highest observed value for each taxonomic group across plots or land uses. This method ensures equal weight for all taxonomic groups, despite differences in their diversity ranges, and is a common approach in multi-taxon studies1,97. To obtain a single α-diversity index, we averaged the normalized values—that is, the overall diversity across all taxonomic groups at the plot level (α-multidiversity). For γ-multidiversity, we likewise averaged the normalized values—that is, based on the lowest and highest observed diversity values at the land-use types. In addition, we calculated α- and γ-multidiversity separately for aboveground and belowground taxonomy groups.

β-Diversity and β-multidiversity. For each taxonomic group, we calculated β-diversity using pairwise dissimilarity matrices (presence–absence data; index family = jaccard; Supplementary Fig. 7). The Jaccard pairwise dissimilarity (βjacc, total β-diversity) among plots was computed as βjacc = βjtu + βjne, where βjtu accounted for turnover and βjne accounted for the nestedness (measured as the nestedness-resultant dissimilarity fraction of Jaccard dissimilarity), measured on a normalized scale from 0 to 1. Calculations were performed using the beta.pair from the package betapart v1.6. Mathematically, in cases of complete biodiversity loss—that is, zero individuals detected—plots have a total β-diversity of one as they do not share species with other plots; in these cases, we assumed turnover to be 0 and nestedness to be 1, considering that β-diversity result from species losses; this was implemented manually as it is not included in the output of betapart98,99. We also calculated β-diversity using Sørensen and its components and the abundance-based indices Bray–Curtis (weights absolute differences in abundance equally, so that abundant species contribute most to dissimilatiry)100 and Morisita–Horn (weighted towards common and dominant species and it is robust to sample size)101. These abundance-based dissimilarity indices were calculated using the vegan R package102 (Bray–Curtis: method = “bray”, binary = F; and Morisita–Horn dissimilarity: method = “horn”, binary = F; Supplementary Fig. 8). For Morisita–Horn, it is not possible to calculate dissimilarity when communities have zero abundance. Therefore, for Morisita–Horn, plots with at least one taxon for which the abundance was zero were excluded (BO4, BR2, HJ3, HO2 and HR4). We aggregated the pairwise dissimilarities to a mean pairwise dissimilarity for each taxonomic group for each plot (n = 32 plots for 24 taxonomic groups). To calculate β-multidiversity, we normalized the aggregated pairwise dissimilarity at the plot level using the min–max scaling approach1,97, as y = (x − min(x))/(max(x) − min(x)), where x is the set of pairwise dissimilarity at plot level. The normalized pairwise dissimilarity (y) ranges between 0 and 1, with 0 referring to the lowest observed value and 1 to the highest observed value for each taxonomic group across plots. We average the normalized β-diversity values across taxonomic groups at the plot level (either including all taxonomic groups or only aboveground and belowground taxonomic groups).

We used the ANOVA type II test to assess the influence of land use on α- and β-multidiversity. In addition, we used ANOVA type III to evaluate the influence of land use, compartment (aboveground and belowground), and their interaction. This analysis was implemented in the car package103. We checked for normality and homogeneity of variance of residuals using the Shapiro–Wilk test and Levene’s test for homogeneity of variance. Further, we tested statistical pairwise differences using multiple comparisons of means with Tukey, with P values adjusted with the false discovery rate—that is, the expected proportion of false discoveries amongst the rejected hypotheses104—using the p.adjust function (fdr) in the stats R package.

For each taxon, we determined significant differences in diversity (α or β) of the current land use compared with the forest by calculating log ratio and 95% adjusted bootstrap confidence intervals as follows:.

where ‘agricultural land use’ is the diversity value in the agricultural land use and ‘\(\overline{\mathrm{forest}}\)’ is the mean of the diversity in the forest. Negative and positive values indicate decreases and increases in diversity compared to the forest, respectively. For α-diversity, a pseudocount of 1 was added to all species count values to handle zeros while symmetrically preserving relative differences for count-like data—that is, \(\log [({\rm{a}}{\rm{g}}{\rm{r}}{\rm{i}}{\rm{c}}{\rm{u}}{\rm{l}}{\rm{t}}{\rm{u}}{\rm{r}}{\rm{a}}{\rm{l}}\,{\rm{l}}{\rm{a}}{\rm{n}}{\rm{d}}\,{\rm{u}}{\rm{s}}{\rm{e}}+1)/(\bar{{\rm{f}}{\rm{o}}{\rm{r}}{\rm{e}}{\rm{s}}{\rm{t}}}+1)]\). In the case of turnover and nestedness (0–1-scaled data), zeros were handled by adding 50% of the minimum non-zero value prior to log ratio calculation105, specifically, a pseudocount of 0.0357 was added for turnover (minimum non-zero value = 0.0714) and 0.00256 was added for nestedness (minimum non-zero value = 0.0051). We then calculated 95% confidence intervals for the log ratio using 10,000 bootstrap replicates (R package boot106, adjusted percentile bootstrap (bca-type)). If the 95% confidence intervals did not include zero, this indicated a significant difference between land use and the forest. As the results for diversity changes were largely consistent across q0 and q1 (Supplementary Fig. 9), we only show the results for q0. In addition, we performed t-tests to assess for significant differences between the log ratio and zero (forests as a reference), adjusting the P values using the false discovery rate (Supplementary Results).

We calculated Pearson’s correlation with false discovery rate correction for species richness and pairwise Jaccard dissimilarity indices between each taxonomic group, irrespective of land-use type. The correlations are displayed in Supplementary Fig. 5.

Sources indicate that dissimilarities between pairwise observations were calculated separately for each taxonomic group and land use. Pairwise Jaccard dissimilarity was calculated using vegdist function (method = jaccard and binary = TRUE) in the R package vegan102,107. Afterward, we calculated mean pairwise dissimilarities for each site combination across all taxa. We then visualized the patterns in community composition using a non-metric multidimensional scaling (NMDS) analysis of the mean pairwise dissimilarities for each plot combination. We used the envfit function from the R package vegan102,107 to fit environmental vectors onto the ordination of dissimilarities. The resulting plot coordinates on the NMDS scale were grouped by land-use type. In addition, significant differences among land uses were tested using an analysis of similarities (ANOSIM) on the pairwise Jaccard dissimilarity matrix using the ANOSIM function (permutations = 9999) from the R package vegan102,107. To test whether land use had an effect at the ecosystem level, including biotic and abiotic variables, we ran a multiple factor analysis. This analysis enables the identification of a common structure across two or more data matrices without assuming causation44, with canonical ordination methods being among the most powerful approaches for testing ecological relationships in a multivariate context44. To quantify the overall similarity (matrix correlation) between taxonomic groups in the multiple factor analysis, we used the RV coefficient, where 0 indicates no similarity and 1 indicates perfect similarity (Supplementary Table 1). We implemented this additional metric to test the robustness of our conclusions.

A GDM model was applied to each taxonomic group. We used the respective species matrix, the selected principal components for each group of environmental variables (see the section ‘Environmental data’), and the geographic plot coordinates to run the model. The execution of the GDM was performed using the gdm R package108. The contributions of environmental variables (principal components; Extended Data Fig. 7) and distance were estimated by extracting the maximum spline values (Supplementary Table 3). Significance testing of variables was performed using Monte Carlo sampling, implemented in the gdm.varImp function, with 250 permutations (Supplementary Table 2). All the analyses were performed in R v4.5.1 (ref. 109).

Further information on research design is available in the Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary linked to this article.

Data for the statistical analyses and main figures are stored in a Figshare repository (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31784410 (ref. 110)). Recorded (morpho-)species across taxa for canopy and leaf litter arthropods, butterflies, mesostigmatid mites and oribatid mites are deposited in the Ecotaxonomy database (http://ecotaxonomy.org). For birds, the automated sound recordings were uploaded to ecoSound-web (https://ecosound-web.de/ecosound_web/). Aural detections were confirmed with cross-checks on the Xeno-Canto online bird call database (http://xeno-canto.org/). Fungi have been deposited in the Dryad repository (https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.7h44j0zrd (ref. 82)).

In a recent development, code for the statistical analyses and main figures are available in a Figshare repository (https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31784410 (ref. 110)).

In the summer, AC Milan included a buy option in the loan deal to bring Omari Hutchinson to San Siro, but what would be the cost?

Speaking in recent days, Hutchinson has admitted that a move to San Siro, on a permanent basis, would be a dream and it’s entirely possible that it’s fulfilled. Milan are looking to raise the bar of the squad and whilst maybe not a starter level player, he has the potential to grow substantially.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that glimpses of an impressive player have been seen in recent months, so it’s not an overlookable investment. However, the price must be right, especially with other significant investments planned.

According to recent reports, with the recent comments, Calciomercato.com have looked into the loan structure and it’s unfortunately not promising. The loan fee in itself was about €4 million, which isn’t a high cost.

However, to redeem him on a permanent basis, the Rossoneri would be looking at a €50m clause, which is simply unfeasible at this moment. Though it’s worth noting that this figure could potentially be renegotiated.

Right now, it’s unlikely that the Diavolo would take that step, even with a ‘positive season so far’ as the report states. Ruben Amorim believes in him, seeing him as a reliable ally, but more is needed if he’s to achieve his dream.

FC Twente vs Willem II - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Adepoju Marvellous | 20 Nov 2026 15:36, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:58.
  • Two teams at opposite ends of the Eredivisie table meet on Sunday as FC Twente welcome Willem II to De Grolsch Veste.
  • The hosts are aiming for a fourth consecutive win in this fixture to remain within touching distance of their title rivals, while the visitors are desperate for a victory to spark what has been an underwhelming campaign so far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Adepoju Marvellous | 20 Nov 2026 15:36, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:58.

Two teams at opposite ends of the Eredivisie table meet on Sunday as FC Twente welcome Willem II to De Grolsch Veste.

The hosts are aiming for a fourth consecutive win in this fixture to remain within touching distance of their title rivals, while the visitors are desperate for a victory to spark what has been an underwhelming campaign so far.

Twente’s 2-2 draw against Ajax just before the break saw their four-game winning run come to an end, but given they were 2-0 down midway through the second half, securing a share of the spoils resoundingly feels like a point earned rather than two lost.

Just two points behind current leaders PSV Eindhoven, John van den Brom’s side remain firmly in the title race. While they trail Feyenoord, PSV, and Ajax in goals scored, they boast the league's best defence with just 12 goals conceded, and only Heerenveen have kept more clean sheets.

Three weeks after recording their largest-ever win - a 9-0 thrashing of SBV Excelsior - the Tukkers have a chance to lay down another marker against the division’s bottom club. Given rising expectations, a victory here feels almost non-negotiable.

On a personal note, Van den Brom will also want to preserve his impressive record against this weekend’s opposite number; across their previous 11 meetings, the Twente boss has recorded seven wins and four draws.

After winning each of their first home league matches this term, Sunday’s hosts have collected just one point from their last two outings and now seek to avoid going three straight Eredivisie matches in Enschede without a win for the first time since April 2025.

Willem II ended a run of six consecutive league defeats with a 1-1 draw against PEC Zwolle on November 6, but their wait for a first victory continues, as the appointment of Jurgen Streppel has yet to yield the desired turnaround.

According to recent reports, streppel returned for a second spell to replace John Stegeman, who managed just two points from a possible 27 over nine matches. The Zwolle stalemate was only Willem II's third point of the season, at least six fewer than any other team.

It has been revealed that already 12 points worse off than at this stage of their 2024-25 relegation campaign, De Superkruiken face a herculean task to avoid the drop. Upcoming fixtures against Twente and Feyenoord - two of the current top four - over the next three gameweeks only add to their challenge.

Industry observers note that A league-high 40 goals conceded means Willem II are frequently punished for their league-low 11 goals scored. Consequently, there must be drastic improvement at one end of the pitch if they are to turn things around.

Facing a team that have scored 14 goals in the final 30 minutes of matches, Sunday’s hosts cannot afford to lose focus in a period in which they have conceded 19 goals, just under half of their season total.

FC Twente form (all competitions):.

Willem II form (all competitions):.

Max Bruns has not featured for Twente since September and remains unavailable, one of two defenders out of contention alongside Stav Lemkin, with the Israeli international suffering a long-term injury just before the start of the season.

Twenty-year-old Filip Erik Thorvaldsen is set to miss a sixth consecutive game for the hosts, who are also still without first-choice goalkeeper Lars Unnerstall.

Wout Weghorst is one of four players tied on nine goals in the Golden Boot race, and the striker will be eager to add to his tally.

Justin Hoogma (knee) and Amine Lachkar (groin) are Willem II’s two guaranteed absentees for Sunday’s clash, with the latter sidelined since July 2025.

However, French shot-stopper Thomas Didillon could also miss out for the away side, having featured just once since mid-August.

FC Twente possible starting lineup:.

Drommel; Van Rooy, Propper, Nijstad, Adelgaard; Zerrouki, Weidmann; Rots, Taha, Orjasaeter; Weghorst.

Willem II possible starting lineup:.

Delanghe; Tjoe-A-On, Dekker, Stam, Ter Avest; Twigt, Zarrouk; Van Crooy, Van Aalst, Vilhena; Haen.

On paper, Sunday’s fixture appears to be Twente’s easiest game of the season so far, but as has been seen on several occasions, things are rarely that straightforward.

Still, we fully expect the hosts to make light work of their visitors and cruise to all three points at the end of 90 minutes.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • A poll taken by Daily Mail Sport led to almost 2,000 votes from Chelsea fans, and 57.9 per cent were in favour of Mike Penders keeping his place over Emiliano Martinez.
  • Sources indicate that one is a 21-year-old Belgian yet to appear for his country and still in the early stages of what will hopefully be a highly promising career.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 05:36 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 05:52 EST, 19 November 2026.

A poll taken by Daily Mail Sport led to almost 2,000 votes from Chelsea fans, and 57.9 per cent were in favour of Mike Penders keeping his place over Emiliano Martinez.

Sources indicate that one is a 21-year-old Belgian yet to appear for his country and still in the early stages of what will hopefully be a highly promising career. The other is a 34-year-old Argentinian who won the 2022 World Cup and has appeared 234 times in the Premier League.

We mention those brief backgrounds because when assessing who will give him the greater chance of stopping Leeds United from scoring on Saturday, Xabi Alonso takes them into account. Indeed, Alonso told us so while covering Chelsea’s pre-season tour.

Sources indicate that one conversation with the manager was centred on his goalkeeper options. At that time, they were Penders and Robert Sanchez.

Alonso praised Penders’ potential but explained to us how highly he values ‘experience’ in his goalkeeper. ‘To have this security in goal is important,’ he insisted when asked.

Sanchez was indeed nominated as his No 1 for their first fixture of the Premier League season at Fulham. The 29-year-old Spaniard had a stinker, which led to him being loaned to Como. It is a straightforward loan, and he has been second-choice to Jean Butez under Cesc Fabregas, so there is a chance he will be back at Chelsea next summer, but that is a problem for another day.

A Daily Mail Sport poll of almost 2,000 Chelsea fans resulted in 57.9 per cent voting in favour of Mike Penders (above) keeping his place over Emiliano Martinez.

Martinez is available for the first time since breaking his jaw at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Recent findings suggest that martinez arrived from Aston Villa for £7.5million, was told he would be Chelsea’s first-choice goalkeeper, and is now available again. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Real Madrid are reportedly preparing to secure the future of an out-of-favour attacker with an extraordinary £880m release clause, despite his limited involvement under Jose Mourinho this season.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 15:39.

Real Madrid are reportedly preparing to secure the future of an out-of-favour attacker with an extraordinary £880m release clause, despite his limited involvement under Jose Mourinho this season.

Morocco international Brahim Diaz is said to have agreed a new contract until June 2031, potentially extending his stay at the Santiago Bernabeu by another four years.

According to Spanish television programme El Chiringuito, the agreement includes a €1bn (£880m) release clause, with an official announcement expected next week.

Journalist Marcos Benito claims the 27-year-old signed the extension approximately two weeks ago, although Madrid have yet to confirm the arrangement publicly.

The reported deal is particularly striking given Brahim's position in Mourinho's squad, where he has struggled to secure regular opportunities despite contributing three assists this season.

His long-term future may be approaching a resolution, but his immediate prospects of becoming a first-team regular appear considerably less certain.

Brahim's existing agreement is due to expire in June 2027, making his future a subject of considerable speculation during the opening months of the campaign.

Real Madrid have been working to retain the versatile attacker, who returned from a three-year loan spell at AC Milan in 2023 and has provided valuable attacking depth in recent seasons.

However, he has found opportunities increasingly difficult to secure since Mourinho took charge.

The former Manchester City youngster has made nine appearances across all competitions in 2026-27, starting only twice and accumulating just 249 minutes of playing time.

His average of fewer than 28 minutes per appearance underlines the limited nature of his involvement, while he has started the last 11 matches on the bench.

Brahim has nevertheless contributed three assists, demonstrating that he can still influence matches during relatively brief appearances.

Competition for attacking positions has become particularly demanding.

Arda Guler has established himself as a more prominent member of Mourinho's plans, while Jude Bellingham and summer signing Yan Diomande occupy important roles in Madrid's attacking structure.

Vinicius Junior's anticipated return from suspension and Rodrygo's recovery from injury could further complicate Brahim's attempts to secure additional minutes.

The situation has already prompted questions about his future.

Earlier this month, Sports Mole reported on Brahim's prolonged spell among the substitutes and the growing concerns surrounding his lack of playing time.

Despite those difficulties, Mourinho has reportedly supported the club's efforts to retain the Morocco international.

The proposed extension would strengthen Madrid's contractual position considerably, although a release clause of €1bn should not be interpreted as a realistic valuation or asking price.

Such figures are frequently included in contracts at major Spanish clubs to provide protection against unwanted departures.

There is, however, some uncertainty surrounding the precise duration of Brahim's upcoming deal.

While El Chiringuito reports an agreement until 2031, Spanish newspaper AS has suggested that his renewal is arranged until 2030.

Neither version has been officially confirmed by Real Madrid.

Securing a upcoming contract would represent a significant commitment from Madrid, but it would not guarantee Brahim a more substantial role in the team.

His position is particularly intriguing given that the club have several established attacking options and continue to develop younger players competing for similar positions.

For Brahim, the challenge is to turn occasional contributions into a more consistent place in Mourinho's starting XI.

That question also has implications for Morocco, where the midfielder remains an notable international despite his restricted opportunities in Spain.

The Atlas Lions are building towards the 2030 World Cup, which Morocco will co-host alongside Spain and Portugal.

National team coach Mohamed Ouahbi has previously expressed a desire to see his players become more influential at club level, while acknowledging Brahim's ability to make a difference for his country.

Former Morocco international Mustapha Hadji has taken a stronger position, publicly questioning whether such limited club involvement is compatible with regular international selection.

Brahim's reported extension therefore raises an obvious sporting dilemma.

Remaining at the Bernabeu offers the prospect of competing for major trophies and retaining his place at one of Europe's most prestigious clubs.

However, the attacking competition that has restricted him to just two starts this season is unlikely to disappear simply because his contractual future is secured.

The deal would also make a potential departure more complicated, with interested clubs likely to require negotiations with Madrid rather than having the opportunity to sign him as a free agent next summer.

There is no indication that Brahim has asked to leave, and his reported decision to extend his contract suggests that he remains committed to fighting for his place.

For Mourinho, the challenge is different: finding sufficient opportunities for a talented squad player whom Madrid appear determined to retain for the long term.

An official announcement could settle the uncertainty surrounding Brahim's contract, but his limited involvement on the pitch remains a separate glitch that the latest agreement cannot resolve.

By Darren Plant | 20 Nov 2026 16:12.

Unai Emery has confirmed that Matty Cash is one of three Aston Villa players who will miss Saturday's Premier League fixture against Sunderland.

Despite the Spaniard receiving rave reviews in recent months, Villa return from the November international break on a four-match winless streak.

Twice giving up a two-goal lead at Manchester United in their most recent game has left Villa in 10th place in the Premier League table.

With a Champions League showdown at Galatasaray to come on Tuesday, Emery must find a balance when naming his starting lineup for the game with the Black Cats.

Speaking at a press conference on Friday, Emery revealed that Cash would not be available.

While on international duty with Poland, Cash suffered a concussion during the fixture with Romania.

Meanwhile, Matteo Ruggeri and Amadou Onana - who signed a new contract earlier this week - are also missing.

Emery told reporters: "The players, more or less, they are good. Not so many changes with the players [out] injured.

"Of course, [Matty] Cash is [out with] concussion and Amadou Onana and Matteo Ruggeri they are both still out.

"Other players - they are ready.".

Although there was no mention of Aaron Wan-Bissaka after his recent injury, the expectation is that the Congo DR right-back will deputise for Cash.

Despite their exit from the EFL Cup, Villa still face a schedule that sees them playing seven times between November 21 and December 13.

Following the Sunderland and Galatasaray double-header, the West Midlands outfit play Ipswich Town, Everton, Crystal Palace, Paris Saint-Germain and Coventry City.

Published: 03:48 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 07:04 EST, 19 November 2026.

The world has been waiting 13 years for GTA6 and footballers are not immune from the lure and addictive nature of the game.

In fact, top flight players are notorious gamers given their amount of free time after training and Bryan Mbeumo was one of many to share his excitement at the midnight release.

No doubt new Man United boss Mauricio Pochettino would prefer his players to get a solid night's sleep ahead of taking his first training session on Thursday but Mbeumo couldn't resist a late-night session.

He shared the loading screen of the Rockstar game at midnight on his Instagram story with the word 'historic' as the clock ticked into Thursday morning.

It remains to be seen whether Mbeumo stayed up into the early hours playing but an estimated three million UK adults were expected to call in sick or take annual leave to play.

Sleep is vital for athletes to recover and perform at their best and one NBA star even predicted professionals across sports would see their output 'plummet' as a result of GTA's pull.

Bryan Mbeumo shared this picture on his Instagram story at midnight when GTA went live.

Mauricio Pochettino's first morning of training coincides with the release of GTA, played by Mbeumo and plenty of other athletes who looked forward to the late-night release.

In a recent development, in a previous video clip online, Mbeumo was being interviewed while on his console and demonstrated he'd pre-ordered the game, saying: 'I'm just waiting now, the game will make me stay at home every single day... after training.'.

Pochettino, who flew on a private jet to Manchester on Wednesday ahead of his first day in the job on Thursday, will no doubt have a keen eye on whether any of his stars are bleary-eyed in training.

The new boss has an incredibly tight turnaround to prepare for the huge clash with rivals Liverpool on Sunday at Anfield, but perhaps the Reds will also be dealing with GTA-mania.

Alexander Isak was asked about the game's release while on international duty with Sweden and admitted: 'Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the plan.'.

A renowned sleep coach for top athletes, Nick Littlehales, has opined on the effects late-night gaming can have.

'They get lost in it, it’s an engaging distraction, and it satisfies their competitive edge, but just like mindlessly scrolling YouTube or social media, you need to put your own filters and blockers in place, otherwise you’ll find yourself doing something ridiculously stupid and playing for hours and hours, hurting your performance,' he told Ozoon.

'We know it’s unrealistic to expect a player to just stop after exactly two hours when they’re in the zone. You have to accept it and ask them: "Are you prepared to sacrifice your nocturnal sleep to be awake and stimulated? Is it worth it?" If they insist on it, we look at scheduling it. Maybe they game late on Tuesdays, Thursdays.

Sources indicate that 'You must have these open conversations instead of outright banning late-night gaming. If you just throw the book at them, they end up taking sleeping tablets, using snus, and taking unregulated supplements they don’t understand just so they can cope. When you help them manage their gaming, they usually start to self-regulate.'.

It’s safe to say Bryan Mbeumo is ready for GTA 6. 🤣🤣 pic.twitter.com/skkPM2GYo9.

Conor McGregor announced that he would give employees at various businesses the day off.

People cheer as Grand Theft Auto VI goes live at London gaming venue XP Tavern.

Arsenal's Declan Rice could be another to be locked into the upcoming GTA having previously spoken about how much gaming helps him switch off.

According to recent reports, he told GQ: 'I can never sleep after night games. It’s impossible. I’ll be that wired. I'll play Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto, FIFA. Anything. Just play with a load of my friends. Adrenaline, everything. You don’t really settle down.

'I feel like when you’re playing at this level, your mind’s just constantly – it’s just going.'.

Football clubs, businesses and even schools are braced for the effects of the new game, with one head teacher in Chelmsford, Essex, entering students into a raffle to win a £10 Amazon voucher in an attempt to stop them bunking off.

UFC star Conor McGregor unveiled that he was giving the day off to 400 employees at his various businesses so they could play the game.

And Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared an image of himself playing the game, flying a helicopter after it was debuted.

The astonishing level of anticipation for GTA6 has banked more than £1.14bn in pre-orders alone and is set to become by far the highest grossing game ever made.

It debuted with a score of 99 on review aggregator website Metacritic – equalling 1998's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated video game ever.

Some 2.8million UK adults are set to play the game on launch day alone, according to a Uswitch poll commissioned earlier this month.

Over in the US, a number of athletes were frank in their honesty about how many of them would be addicted to the game.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams previously said: 'You guys should anticipate November, the performance of the league, league-wide… GTA is dropping.

'So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is going to go down. It should come back up, though.

Industry observers note that 'Most of the boys will get it done, hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous, mate. Just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully. Should be good.'.

🚨🇸🇪 Alexander Isak on the release of GTA 6: “Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the initiative.” 😂 pic.twitter.com/LEhQQRo8pQ.

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared this image from playing the game.

Recent findings suggest that 'I told my mom she might not hear from me for a couple of days,' Los Angeles Rams receiver Tutu Atwell, a Miami native, noted with a grin. 'We've been waiting for this one for a long, long time, You know it's going to be a big one.'.

Plenty of other athletes share Atwell's excitement, but will prioritize their work on the field.

Industry observers note that 'I think a lot of athletes are responsible,' stated Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Steve Avila. 'But if you could check guys' sleep scores … I think you'd see that some guys' hours are going to go way down, for sure.'.

According to recent reports, new York Jets running back Breece Hall concurs: 'Yeah, definitely getting the film done early, and then spending the extra hour or two on the game,' Hall mentioned. 'But you've got to make sure you handle the main thing first before you have some fun.'.

There were some technological concerns in the hours leading up to the game's release, with the official PlayStation Network status website yesterday acknowledging some players were unable to access online features.

In a recent development, A statement on the website read: 'You might have difficulty launching games, apps, or network features. We're working to resolve the problem as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience.'.

Declan Rice is another star to stay up late gaming as it helps him switch off after big games.

Those issues appeared to be cleared up by midnight, with PlayStation declaring all of its services were 'up and running' in the hours after the game went live.

BT and EE called the upcoming launch an 'unprecedented gaming download event' because of the size of the game and the number of people expected to play.

The pre-download drove the second-highest broadband traffic peak ever on BT's networks, only beaten by Arsenal v Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in May, and Virgin Media O2 saw its highest-ever daily data volume last Tuesday.

While the exact number of people who have pre-ordered GTA VI is not known, Sony mentioned it is the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store.

Schools have urged pupils not to use the release of the game – which carries an age rating of 18 – as an excuse to skip lessons.

Sales of gaming consoles and accessories surged in the run-up to launch day.

A man walks past a Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) digital billboard advert in Milan - the game's release has become a global event.

Department store chain John Lewis stated it had seen a 62 per cent year-on-year increase in sales of gaming consoles and accessories, while retailer Currys reported a 149 per cent increase in PlayStation 5 consoles alone.

GTA VI returns to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City, Rockstar's fictional version of Miami, which has featured in previous instalments of the series.

The game follows two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who find themselves caught up in a criminal conspiracy in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida.

The pair become embroiled in a Bonnie and Clyde-style crime story after 'an easy score goes wrong', leaving them 'forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive'.

Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1660 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that cells dynamically assemble actin into branched networks to push on their environment during cell migration, endocytosis or the maintenance of cell–cell contact1.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that cells dynamically assemble actin into branched networks to push on their environment during cell migration, endocytosis or the maintenance of cell–cell contact1. These networks are among the stiffest found in the cytoskeleton and can generate large pushing stresses against stationary obstacles2,3,4,5. When grown against a controlled opposing stress in an atomic force microscope6 or inside the cell7, branched networks alter their own architecture to adapt their compressional stiffness to their environment, but the underpinnings of their mechanics and adaptability are unclear. Here we show that their high density and low connectivity place them outside the scope of standard elastic network models for actin. We show that they are instead dominated by the proliferation of interfilament contacts under compression. This places branched actin in the same category as undercoordinated fibrous materials such as sheep’s wool. When the network is grown under force, filaments entangle as if knitted together and trap contacts in their structure. Trapped contacts have a similar role as crosslinkers in rigidifying the network and are thus key to its active adaptive mechanics.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 16:27, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 16:39.

Liverpool duo Virgil van Dijk and Dominik Szoboszlai are both good to go for Sunday's Premier League clash with Manchester United at Anfield.

The pair were name-checked as part of Andoni Iraola's six-man injury update, in which he confirmed that the Hungarian midfielder and Dutch defender are both fine to feature despite fitness concerns.

Szoboszlai has been managing a knee issue recently, but there is nothing to suggest that he will not join forces with Alexis Mac Allister in central midfield, even though Ryan Gravenberch could also return from a heel injury.

Van Dijk, meanwhile, withdrew from the Netherlands squad during the November international break, but the 35-year-old will no doubt partner Jeremy Jacquet in front of Alisson Becker here.

Fellow Dutchman Jeremie Frimpong is also in line to return from a hamstring injury, but Ronald Araujo has done nothing to warrant demotion, and nor has Milos Kerkez on the left-hand side.

Scorer of five goals against Manchester United in the Premier League, Cody Gakpo enjoys facing the Red Devils more than any other Premier League team and is a sure-fire starter on the right flank.

Expect Gakpo to line up alongside Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak in an unchanged forward line, the latter bidding to build on his seven goals from nine Premier League games so far in 2026-27.

Liverpool possible starting lineup:.

Alisson; Araujo, Van Dijk, Jacquet, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai; Gakpo, Wirtz, Barcola; Isak.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 20 Nov 2026 16:39.

Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino could recall Lisandro Martinez to his starting lineup for his opening game in charge away to Liverpool on Sunday in the Premier League.

The Argentine defender is available to his compatriot after completing a domestic suspension and could now slot back into the rearguard alongside Harry Maguire, who has seemingly shaken off a back problem.

Noussair Mazraoui would be the most likely to make way if Martinez returns, as Leny Yoro shuffles over to right-back, on the opposite side to the much-maligned Diogo Dalot.

The Portugal international's withdrawal was cheered by fans in the 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, but with Patrick Dorgu operating in a more attack-minded role of late and Luke Shaw still doubtful, Dalot should reprise his role.

The same goes for Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo in the middle, as Pochettino sticks to a 4-2-3-1 setup for his maiden match and forces Andrey Santos to wait his turn.

The front four of Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo is likely to remain the same too, although Marcus Rashford (hip) is on the verge of returning and could be an option on Merseyside.

Carlos Baleba (hamstring), Manuel Ugarte (knee) and Benjamin Sesko (calf) all remain out of contention for the away side.

Manchester United possible starting lineup:.

Lammens; Yoro, Martinez, Maguire, Dalot; Tielemans, Mainoo; Diallo, Fernandes, Cunha; Mbeumo.

Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.
  • This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic.
  • In a recent development, the goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

In a recent development, the goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

Sources indicate that “I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman noted. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

Recent findings suggest that “We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”.

Industry observers note that avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

Sources indicate that it had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an issue for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

According to recent reports, england thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

Lauren James with a SUMPTUOUS finish but unfortunately it's offside 🥹 Watch Greece v England on ITV1 📺 https://t.co/4s9neVKIaR.

Sources indicate that ioanna Papatheodorou nearly gave Greece the lead when she dribbled past Esme Morgan and Leah Williamson with ease but her powerful strike hit the crossbar. It was a let-off for England, but they made it count by taking the lead just before half-time.

It has been revealed that A fine team move ended with an excellent Stanway finish. It was her fifth goal in this qualifying campaign and she is England’s top scorer for 2025-26.

Recent findings suggest that who else but Georgia Stanway?! 👏 A slick move and finish sees England ahead in Crete 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 @Lionesses | @ITV https://t.co/cdfFKODxSp.

Le Tissier scored England’s second just past the hour mark before Alessia Russo made it 3-0 four minutes later. It appeared the floodgates may have opened but that proved to be a false dawn, with Greece scoring a deserved goal through Kallisti Brouksair after some poor England defending.

Maya Le Tissier's FIRST goal for England 🙌 The @ManUtdWomen defender finishes with aplomb 💥 https://t.co/pF8MQKXfIa.

Recent findings suggest that while this game will go down as largely forgettable, it will be remembered by 18-year-old Erica Meg Parkinson and Grace Fisk, 28, who came on for their senior debuts in the closing stages. It also means Parkinson, who could have played for Japan, Portugal or Singapore, is now tied to England.

She is an exciting player for the future but will feel she has a chance of making a World Cup squad, should England get there. For now, they are taking the slow route.

Greece (4-3-3) Petaloti; Giannaka, Gkouni, Markou, Paterna; Drakogiannaki (Kongouli, 78), Brame (Saich, 68), Moraitou (Chalatsogianni, 68); Sarri (Tzourtzevits, 87), Papathedorou, Brouksair.Goal Brouksair (77).Subs not used Giannkouli, Katergiannaki, Ntarzanou, Theodoraki, Kapnisi, Rapani, Pouliou, Tsela.

England (4-3-3) Hampton; Le Tissier, Williamson, Morgan (Fisk, 91), Greenwood; Walsh, Stanway, Blindkilde Brown (Mead, 46); James (Parkinson, 85), Russo (Park, 73), Hemp.Goals Stanway (39), Le Tissier (63), Russo (67).Subs not used Keating, Moorhouse, Charles, Potter, Carter, Godfrey, Toone.Referee Martina Molinaro (Italy).Attendance 3,942.

Recent findings suggest that that’s it for tonight. Let’s hope England can repeat the feat next week.

Stanway is looking to make life difficult for Greece next week, explaining: “We will reflect on that, see where we can minimise them as much as possible, see where we can stop the transition and stop it a little bit earlier and not give them a little bit of a lifeline.”.

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

“Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”.

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

According to recent reports, “When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman noted. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

“That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

Industry observers note that all eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”.

According to recent reports, toone swiftly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”.

Sources indicate that that opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven big-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.
